# Exception audit

Every `catch` in `src/**` (637 sites) after the exception-visibility change. A snapshot of that lane (2026-10-12): files and line numbers have moved since (for example `PlayerbotLocalPlanner.cs` was removed with the goal policy in 1202eb2bd, so its rows keep the `src/ArcaneCore.World/Playerbots/` path it had); rerun the script for the current tree.

**Method and limits.** The table is generated by `scripts/exception-audit/audit.py` (rerun: `py -3 scripts/exception-audit/audit.py . <base-ref>`). It reads each catch body with regular expressions and classifies it from that text alone. The verdicts are heuristic and **unverified**: no compiler or test checked them, and "propagated" or "by-design" means the body looks that way, not that the caller was followed. A reason in quotation marks is the comment found at the site. FIXED is a site whose body changed in this lane and now logs the exception object.

Policy: an unexpected exception is logged with its object at Error (the console shows type, message, stack trace and inner exceptions) and counted in the `FaultLedger` (`.server faults`); Warning is for expected, recoverable conditions; shutdown and cancellation and documented parse fallbacks are swallowed. Text that may hold a secret (bot chat, GitHub publishing) is deliberately logged as the exception type only.

## Counts

| Verdict | Sites |
|---|---|
| logged | 239 |
| FIXED | 27 |
| ledger-only | 16 |
| propagated | 131 |
| message-only | 5 |
| by-design | 219 |
| total | 637 |

## Fire-and-forget and unobserved tasks

About 115 sites (`_ = Task.Run`, `_ = XAsync()`, `ContinueWith`, background consumers) were listed by pattern; the queue consumers catch and log inside their loop, so they appear in the table. A fault that still goes unobserved reaches `TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException`, which `CrashHandler` logs at Critical with the full exception. Fixed here: the `.playerbot` command lambdas (`PlayerbotCommands`, `PlayerbotFleetCommands`, `PlayerbotScenarioCommands`), `.reload`, `.hotcode refresh` and the hot module commands answered the GM with a type or message and lost the exception; they now log it (`ManagedPlayerbotFeature.ReportCommandFault`, `CommandFaultLogging`). There is no `async void` in `src/**`. The per-site follow-through of each task was not audited.
